signature: allow = every ue-mcp category (32), deny = nothing
summary: The rig policy allows every ue-mcp category plus the flow tool and denies nothing: all 3,714 actions and flows are reachable, including the escape hatches (execute_python, execute_command, console, invoke_*), builds, C++ writes, plugins, Fab, flows, feedback and source control. The owner opened it on 2026-11-14.
constraints: Decisions are on category.method; deny always wins.
The live copy is C:\ProgramData\watoom\ue-mcp-policy.json on the rig, re-read on every request.
A category added by a later ue-mcp release is not allowed until the policy is regenerated and reviewed.

Allowed does not mean harmless: prefer the dedicated action over an escape hatch, read before you change, and do not run builds, plugin installs or source-control actions unless the task asks for them.

summary: No action is denied by the WatooM policy, so a refusal does not come from it. A refusal then comes from ue-mcp itself (its guards in the project's ue-mcp.yml, a read-only session mode, a modal dialog blocking the editor, or an Input validation error).
constraints: Read the refusal text: dialogBlocking, WRITE_BLOCKED, a guard name or a validation message each have a different fix.
Do not retry a refused call unchanged.

signature: refused -> report the exact text, do not work around
summary: If a call is refused, report the category.method and the exact refusal text in the handoff; do not retry in a loop, rename the call, or use another route to reach the editor.
constraints: Opening or closing an action is an operator decision on the rig.
